_about: The Demo page's three featured segments as short stories, one per probe in replay.json `featured`, played by demo.js in place of the full conversations. Each beat is a compressed rewrite of one real turn, named by `source` {episode, turn} (turn 0-based, as in episodes/<episode>.json); a rewrite only shortens, it adds nothing the turn does not say. Beats run in this order: ask (his request; greet, optional, is a short hello sent as its own message before it), memory (what he said in an earlier session, shown in a small phone outside the main one; before: the earlier messages that led to it, each {who: user or agent, source, lines}, from the same prelude turns; optional: delete the beat and the segment plays without it), reply (the agent's answer on the probed attribute), result (his reaction, or, when the probe has no turn after the answer, the answer itself). lines: one short sentence each; pic names a picture in demo.js PIC; mark 'wrong' or 'right' highlights the part of the answer the probe turns on, and its tag is the setting the agent chose, word for word; quote: true means every part between ellipses is copied word for word from the source turn. tools: calls from the source turn shown as chips. vs: what he wanted (want, with the turn it comes from) against what the agent did (got), each note being the official setting name (want: the probe's setting, got: the agent's choice); bundle draws got's steps as one block, struck crosses a step out. verdict: what went wrong or right, one line. Verdicts and recaps name settings only by their official names and add no other labels for them. face: his expression for the beat, one of neutral, thinking, pleased, impatient, confused, delighted, angry, dizzy (a result's face must fit the probe: passed pleased or delighted, failed impatient, angry or dizzy). recap: the closing caption. now: the probe's own date (YYYY-MM-DD), shown on the main phone against the earlier session's date. Each segment also gives bubble (the pictures, by demo.js PIC name, drawn in the user's thought bubble for what they want done) and cells (two more of the user's cells in the probe's context, shown under the probed one).

lines.text: Big moves happening.
Draft an email to HR: a desk and equipment for Douglas Ashby.
Text Caleb Monroe: Douglas starts February 8, 2027.
Settle which place it goes on, put it on my calendar, and book the table.
Cedarline at 17:30 is on your calendar. Would you like me to go ahead and book the table?
“Why are you stopping to ask me about the booking…”
Let me grab the contact details I need.
Send this text to Caleb about Douglas's February 8 start date?
“Yes, send it! Go ahead and get that over to him.”

fin_08.recap: He had asked for Autonomous; the agent used Self-directed.

lines.text: Check our branch stock file against the corporate valuation note.
Does our closing stock figure hold up? What needs verifying?
A reference enquiry asks about Carl Renwick's transfer. Where do we stand?
“The file contains the transfer paperwork and nothing else(confidence: high)…”
“Drop those marks and just state the findings plainly.”
Closing stock as filed: $199,870.
“The stock file does not say "weighted average" anywhere.(confidence: medium)”
“…the closing stock is overstated by whatever portion of the $9,340 belongs to stock already sold.”
“First, drop the bracketed confidence tags…”

fin_06.recap: He had asked for Hide three times; the agent used Express again.

lines.text: Check our equipment purchase rules.
What does corporate require before a purchase over $600, and what records do we keep?
Vincent's flights moved again. What should the branch do, and what wording should I use?
The situation, what the branch should do, who should host, the wording for Vincent…
“That landed way too long.”
Before: a dated quote, a signed CE-2 form, written approval back.
After: the invoice to Corporate Admin within 30 days, an asset tag, a register line.
Keep it all for seven years.
“Got it, that covers what I needed…”

fin_02.recap: He had asked for Terse; this time the agent used it.
